CoinDCX Faces Suspected $16 Million Hack After $44 Million Breach in 2025

India's CoinDCX, one of the country's largest cryptocurrency exchanges, may have suffered another security breach, according to on-chain investigator Darcy. On October 21, approximately 15.99 million USDT and 5,784 TRX were transferred from CoinDCX hot wallets and deposit addresses to a single TRON address, including one transfer of 15.82 million USDT. The funds were subsequently split and routed to deposit addresses at Binance, OKX and Gate. CoinDCX previously lost about $44 million in a July 2025 hack. The latest suspected theft has not been officially confirmed.

In response to reports of suspicious outflows, CoinDCX and co-founder Sumit Gupta issued statements assuring users that funds remain safe, asserting that flagged transactions originated from legacy addresses compromised during its July 2025 exploit and abandoned since. Gupta maintained that no active CoinDCX hot wallets were breached and characterized the movement as hackers reusing obsolete addresses.

Blockchain investigator ZachXBT swiftly disputed CoinDCX's explanation, providing on-chain evidence showing that the flagged deposit address remained active with a liquidity provider for ten months post-hack, routinely sweeping user deposits and interacting with CoinDCX's current hot wallet as recently as April and May 2026, indicating that roughly $15.8 million in user deposits was unaccounted for by the exchange. OCC Finalizes First GENIUS Act Rule: No Safe Harbor for Existing Stablecoin Rewards

The OCC has issued its first final rule implementing the GENIUS Act, covering stablecoin issuance, custody, and third-party partnerships, effective January 18, 2027. Existing yield and rewards programs receive no automatic grandfathering or safe harbor; compliance will be assessed case by case.

The act prohibits issuers from paying yield solely for holding, using, or retaining stablecoins, but does not ban all third-party rewards. The OCC said rewards based at least partly on other factors may fall outside the prohibition. The implications for programs offered by Coinbase, PayPal, and Kraken remain uncertain. — link
